title: The Principle of Superposition in Quantum Theory
text:
Quantum mechanics posits that subatomic particles do not possess definite states until they are measured. Instead, a particle exists in a superposition—a combination of all possible states simultaneously.

The act of observation forces the wave function to collapse, meaning the system is instantaneously reduced from its myriad possibilities into a single, measurable state. This fundamental relationship between measurement and reality remains one of the most counterintuitive aspects of modern physics.
